title: India's land borders at a glance
summary: Seven neighbours, about 15,107 km of land border, and the forces that guard each stretch.
body: India's land border is about 15,106.7 km long and touches seven countries. Its coastline, including the islands, is about 7,516 km by the older count; a 2023–24 remeasurement put it at about 11,098 km.

- Bangladesh: 4,096.7 km. Guarded by the BSF.
- China: 3,488 km. Guarded by the ITBP.
- Pakistan: 3,323 km. Guarded by the BSF.
- Nepal: 1,751 km. Guarded by the SSB (Sashastra Seema Bal).
- Myanmar: 1,643 km. Guarded by the Assam Rifles.
- Bhutan: 699 km. Guarded by the SSB.
- Afghanistan: 106 km, in the area under Pakistani occupation.

- Radcliffe Line: India–Pakistan and India–Bangladesh boundaries drawn in 1947.
- Line of Control (LoC): the de facto line in Jammu and Kashmir.
- Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL): the Siachen sector.
- Line of Actual Control (LAC): India–China.
- McMahon Line: India's position in the eastern sector with China.
Most border with Bangladesh: West Bengal. Sikkim borders three countries: China, Nepal and Bhutan.
